stem: To be recognized as national Party in India, a party must have secured at least how much percentage of votes in the previous election at least?

options.label: a
options.text: 10 percent of valid votes in four or more States

options.label: b
options.text: 4 percent of valid votes in four or more States

options.label: c
options.text: 15 percent of valid votes in four or more States

options.label: d
options.text: 6 percent of valid votes in more than half of the States

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: According to the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 (as amended), the Election Commission recognizes a political party as a National Party only if any one of the following three conditions is fulfilled— (а) The candidates set up by the party, in any four or more States, at the last general election to the Lok Sabha (House of the People) or to the Legislative Assembly of the State concerned, secure not less than 6 percent of the total valid votes polled in each of those States at that general election; and, in addition, the party returns at least four members to the Lok Sabha at the said general election from any State or States. (b) At the last general election to the Lok Sabha, the party wins at least 2 percent of the total number of seats in the Lok Sabha (any fraction exceeding one-half being counted as one); and the party’s candidates are elected to that House from not less than three States. (с) The party is recognized as a State Party in at least four States.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Aam Aadmi Party is now a National Party. On the basis of the Gujarat Legislative Assembly election results declared in December 2022, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) claimed recognition as a National Party on the ground that it had acquired the qualification of a State-level party in four States. In this regard, as per the information issued by the Election Commission in April 2023, it has been granted the status of a National Party. At present, option (b) is the correct answer.

stem: name the political party which is not a part of a composite central government, but their member has been elected speaker of the thirteenth lok Sabha.
expl: G.M.C. Balayogi was elected Speaker in the Twelfth Lok Sabha and also served as Speaker in the Thirteenth Lok Sabha; he was a member of the Telugu Desam Party. This party did not join the coalition government of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).
